rules.title: `_` and empty name are non-binding wildcards
rules.statement: A wildcard pattern named `_` (or unnamed) introduces no binding and reserves no slot; any other name in a wildcard position is a binding that reserves a fresh dense slot.

rules.title: Or-pattern alternatives share binding slots; distinct patterns start fresh
rules.statement: Within one top-level pattern, repeated binding names across or-pattern alternatives map to the SAME dense slot; binding-slot allocation is reset at the start of each top-level pattern, so separate match arms / let patterns allocate independent slots.

rules.title: Prelude variant shorthand in patterns
rules.statement: Unqualified variant patterns `Some`/`None`/`Ok`/`Err` resolve to `Option`/`Result` variants when no enum qualifier is given and the prelude enum carries that variant.

rules.title: `use Type.{V,..}` bare-variant alias resolves in patterns
rules.statement: A bare (unqualified) variant name in a pattern resolves to its enum when that name was imported via a `use Type.{V, ...}` variant-alias.

rules.title: Type-alias to enum peels in variant patterns
rules.statement: A variant pattern `Alias::V` / `Alias::V(..)` where `type Alias<..> = Enum<..>` resolves the variant on the underlying enum; alias type-arguments do not affect which variant matches.

rules.title: Unknown enum / variant in pattern is an error
rules.statement: A variant pattern naming an enum not in scope, or a variant not declared by the resolved enum, is rejected.

rules.title: Variant pattern enum must equal scrutinee enum
rules.statement: When the scrutinee has a concrete enum type, a variant pattern naming a different enum is rejected.

rules.title: Bare `Foo(a,b)` tuple-struct pattern destructures positional fields
rules.statement: An unqualified call-form pattern `Foo(p0, p1, ...)` whose name resolves to a tuple-struct destructures it as a struct pattern with synthetic positional field names "0","1",...; sub-pattern j binds field j.

rules.title: Tuple-struct pattern arity must match (absent `..`)
rules.statement: Without a `..` rest, a tuple-struct pattern must supply exactly as many sub-patterns as the struct's field count; with `..`, the supplied count must not exceed the arity.

rules.title: At most one `..` rest per tuple/tuple-struct pattern
rules.statement: A tuple-struct or tuple-variant pattern may contain at most one `..` rest; sub-patterns before the rest bind low positions and those after bind tail positions, with skipped positions binding nothing.

rules.title: Match ergonomics peel all &/&mut/* layers
rules.statement: Pattern matching peels all `&`, `&mut`, and `*` layers of the scrutinee type to obtain the concrete payload shape, so a pattern over `&&Enum<T>` (arbitrary depth) unifies against the inner `Enum<T>`.

rules.title: Default binding modes wrap payload bindings by reference
rules.statement: Under a `&`/`&mut` scrutinee, every plain named payload binding binds by-reference: the binding type is wrapped in `&`/`&mut` once per scrutinee ref-layer, with the outermost layer carrying mut iff any peeled layer was `&mut`. Bindings to `_` and synthesized slots are exempt.
rules.divergence: Rust-conformant (RFC 2005); historical move-only-type restriction now lifted

rules.title: `ref`/`ref mut` payload binding wraps type in &/&mut
rules.statement: An explicit `ref v` (resp. `ref mut v`) sub-pattern in a variant payload binds by reference: the binding type is wrapped in `&` (resp. `&mut`), binding the payload slot's address rather than a load. Explicit ref overrides default-binding-mode wrapping.

rules.title: Generic enum type-args substitute into payload binding types
rules.statement: For a generic enum scrutinee `Enum<A,..>`, each variant payload binding's type is the declared payload type with the enum's type parameters substituted by the scrutinee's type-arguments (after peeling ref/ptr layers).

rules.title: Struct-shape variant pattern resolves fields by name
rules.statement: A `E::V { f0, f1: p, .. }` pattern is allowed only for struct-shaped variants; named fields resolve to payload positions, shorthand `f` binds field `f` to name `f`, an unknown or duplicate field name is an error, and absent `..` every field must be specified.

rules.title: Tuple-shape variant rejects brace pattern
rules.statement: A tuple-shaped variant (positional payload, no field names) cannot be matched with brace `{ .. }` pattern syntax.

rules.title: Nested variant inner pattern lowers to a synthesized guard
rules.statement: A nested variant inner pattern (e.g. `Some(Color::Red)`, `Some(Some(v))`) binds the outer payload to a synthetic name and gates the arm with a synthesized `match synth { <inner> => <check>, _ => false }`; binding-carrying inners additionally re-extract their bindings in the arm body via a let-else, composing to arbitrary depth.
rules.divergence: A — guarded nested-variant arms need a catch-all for exhaustiveness (DIVERGENCES.md: finite-enum coverage of guarded arms not yet proven)

rules.title: Range inner pattern lowers to `>= && <=` guard
rules.statement: A range inner pattern `V(lo..=hi)` (or `V(n @ lo..hi)`) binds the payload to `synth`/the @-name and gates the arm with `synth >= lo && synth <= hi`; an exclusive `lo..hi` lowers to `lo..=(hi-1)`. Under by-ref ergonomics the synth is dereferenced for the comparison.

rules.title: Literal inner pattern lowers to `==` guard (str via str_eq)
rules.statement: An int/neg-int/bool/char literal inner pattern binds the payload to `synth` and gates the arm with `synth == <literal>`; a string literal inner gates with `str_eq(synth, "..")` rather than pointer-comparing slices.

rules.title: `n @ sub` binds payload and applies sub-pattern guard
rules.statement: An `@`-binding `n @ <sub>` in a variant payload binds the payload to name `n` and additionally gates the arm with the refutable guard of `<sub>` (range/literal/variant) built against `n`; `n @ _` binds with no guard.

rules.title: Or-pattern inner must be bindingless
rules.statement: An or-pattern inner `V(A | B)` is lowered to a `match synth { A | B => true, _ => false }` guard only if every alternative binds nothing (literals, unit variants, bindingless-data variants, or a bare wildcard `_`); a binding-carrying alternative is rejected.

rules.title: Match ergonomics excludes raw pointers
rules.statement: Binding-carrying nested-variant patterns over a raw-pointer (`*const`/`*mut`) scrutinee are rejected; match ergonomics (by-ref binding) applies only to `&`/`&mut`.

rules.title: Irrefutable nested struct/tuple payload destructures in arm body
rules.statement: A nested struct- or tuple-pattern inside a variant payload binds the payload to a synthetic slot and emits an irrefutable `let <sub> = __synth;` destructure as an arm-body prologue.

rules.title: Named binding against unit-typed payload is a zero-sized local
rules.statement: When a variant's payload types are all `()`, a `_` binding is dropped and a named binding is kept with a `()` binding type (a zero-sized local in scope), since unit fields are elided from the enum layout. The unit payload position itself is omitted from binding types.

rules.title: Variant payload binding count must match payload arity
rules.statement: The number of payload bindings in a variant-data pattern must equal the number of (non-unit) payload types of the variant.

rules.title: `()` unit sub-pattern binds nothing
rules.statement: A `()` (unit) sub-pattern in a variant payload position introduces no binding.
